rv.q: Both actors are exceptional–but Hill is on a par with John Leguizamo, which is as praiseworthy as we get.

The virtuosity of their performances is always subtle, making the evening seem as effortless as breezing down to the local pub for a beer and to exchange wild tales with two of your more outrageous friends.

cn.t: This Irish comedy about Hollywood filming on location charms with its two-actor ensemble tackling multiple roles, though it stumbles with a precious opening and struggles to balance its light comedic tone with darker dramatic ambitions.

vs.sum: The John Golden Theatre offers good sightlines from most seats, though sound quality can vary, especially under the mezzanine. Seating comfort is typical of older theaters with tight legroom, but the venue maintains a pleasant ambiance overall. Facilities are adequate, though not exceptional.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No wheelchair-accessible restroom (use adjacent Schoenfeld).
